stem.text: The mass of a block of melting ice, measured in kilograms, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function M of time t, measured in minutes. It is known that \( M'(9) = 6.5 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( M'(9) = 6.5 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 9 minutes, the mass of the block of ice is increasing at a rate of 6.5 kilograms per minute.

worked_solution.text: \( M'(9) \) is the rate of change of the mass of the block of ice at the instant t = 9, so it is measured in kilograms per minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: derivative as a rate of change

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so the mass of the block of ice is increasing at that instant, by 6.5 kilograms for each minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction

options.label: Over the first 9 minutes, the mass of the block of ice is increasing at a rate of 6.5 kilograms per minute.
options.derivation: the instant replaced by the whole interval up to it, so the interpretation no longer says when the rate holds

options.label: At time t = 9 minutes, the mass of the block of ice is increasing at a rate of 6.5 kilograms per minute.
At time t = 9 minutes, the mass of the block of ice is increasing at a rate of 6.5 minutes per kilogram.
options.derivation: the units assembled the wrong way round, time units over quantity units

options.label: At time t = 9 minutes, the mass of the block of ice has changed by a total of 6.5 kilograms.
options.derivation: the derivative value read as an amount, the total change in the quantity, rather than a rate
